core_obligations: Verify that the morphism is quasi-separated so that the definition of the normalization in Y applies: Y is quasi-separated as a locally algebraic scheme, and quasi-separatedness of the source makes the morphism quasi-separated (proof lines 4978-4984).
Apply the general finiteness theorem for normalizations in Nagata schemes, using that locally algebraic schemes are locally Noetherian and Nagata (proof lines 4984-4989).
proof_roadmap: Finiteness from the Nagata case (proof lines 4984-4989).
difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact morphism f: Y to X of locally algebraic schemes over a field k with Y reduced, the lemma shows that the normalization X' of X in Y is finite over X (statement lines 4969-4975). The proof first verifies that the definition of the normalization in Y applies in this setting: Y is quasi-separated because locally algebraic schemes over a field are locally Noetherian, hence so is the morphism, so the definition is available (proof lines 4978-4984). Finiteness then follows from the general finiteness statement for normalizations in Nagata schemes, using that locally algebraic schemes are locally Noetherian and Nagata (proof lines 4984-4989). The claim is H2: two checks of hypotheses plus one cited finiteness theorem, with the local algebraicity being used twice for different purposes.
